importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is large — NVPH, shade net house, fan-and-pad, tunnel, and polycarbonate structures are visually distinct. Buyers use the image to identify structure type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Pipe diameter, frame coating (HDG vs powder coat), and structure type are NHB/MIDH subsidy-compliance gates. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for government scheme eligibility, which is the primary purchase driver for the majority buyer segment.

Per sq mt rate is the primary comparison metric for Indian farmer buyers operating within government subsidy cost benchmarks. Price varies substantially across structure types (basic tunnel vs fan-and-pad vs polycarbonate), so buyers compare prices only after confirming spec and type match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per project (small installations) or per guntha (used structures) — without unit shown, per sq mt price cannot be compared across listings. Per sq mt is the NHB/MIDH subsidy evaluation standard and must always accompany price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared without unit — per sq mt vs per project vs per guntha creates real confusion. Unit ambiguity directly undermines the buyer's ability to compare quotes across sellers.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand with buyer recall in Indian greenhouse structures — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and turnkey contractors; buyers search by spec, subsidy eligibility, and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: NHB empanelment status, installation track record, and state-specific subsidy processing experience are evaluated during vendor selection but only after spec and price shortlisting. Company is a qualifier, not a primary discovery signal.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental product class (NVPH vs fan-and-pad vs shade net vs tunnel) — values are non-interchangeable and carry the largest price delta in the category, with fan-and-pad structures costing three to five times more than basic tunnel frames.

Hot Dip Galvanized (HDG) coating is the NHB/MIDH subsidy-qualifying standard — this spec is a hard compliance gate that determines subsidy eligibility and carries a significant price premium over powder-coated or paint-coated alternatives.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The cladding type (UV polyethylene film vs polycarbonate sheet vs shade net) is a primary product differentiator that determines crop suitability, light transmission, and cost tier — buyers and subsidy schemes treat these as distinct product categories.

NHB/MIDH subsidy compliance mandates a minimum 200-micron UV-stabilised film — buyers must verify this spec to confirm subsidy eligibility, and sellers use it to differentiate compliant from non-compliant offerings.

NHB/MIDH subsidy specifications require a minimum 275 GSM zinc coating on HDG pipes — this is a distinct compliance parameter from Frame Coating type and is the most commonly audited spec during government scheme inspections.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental product type and climate control approach — sellers need this to determine which product line applies, whether active cooling equipment is included, and what the correct price tier is.
Project scale determines total material quantity and cost — sellers cannot generate a meaningful quote without knowing the covered area requirement.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires UV polyethylene film, polycarbonate sheet, or shade net to confirm product fit and provide an accurate price — a polycarbonate greenhouse costs three to five times more than a UV film polyhouse of the same area.
